title: Credential
description: A declared credential anchored to an external authority's public register — a license, certification, or permit the SELLER declares and any reader verifies against the authority's own record. The designer pins WHICH register the assembly credentials against (a URI template whose {id} placeholder substitutes the declared identifier); the seller declares their identifier once on their profile, and checkout folds it onto the committed leaf. The register — the authority's public record, distinct from the protocol's on-chain registries — is the source of truth: the clause references it, it does not restate, fetch, or interpret it. Verification is the reader's act at read time (a per-leaf affordance opens the substituted register URL); nothing gates signing, and no verification status is stored — the bond prices a false or lapsed declaration, and the committed claim is timestamped evidence for the composed recourse layer. Example register template: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/xjfq-wh2d.json?license_number={id} (the NYC TLC active for-hire drivers register).

fields.name: credentialRegisterUri
fields.label: Authority register (URI template)
fields.description: The external authority's public register, as a URI template with an {id} placeholder for the declared identifier. Pinned by the designer as a specific term — part of the assembly's tailored identity. The register is the authority's own record; the protocol never mirrors or interprets it.

fields.name: credentialTitle
fields.label: Credential
fields.description: Human-readable name of the credential the register attests (e.g. "NYC TLC For-Hire Vehicle Driver License"). Pinned by the designer; labels drawers and derived documents.

fields.name: credentialId
fields.label: Declared identifier
fields.description: The seller's declared identifier in the authority's register (e.g. a TLC license number). Authored once on the seller's profile and folded onto the leaf at checkout; substituted into the register template's {id} for verification by any reader.
